properties.snippet: This feature layer, utilizing National Geospatial Data Asset (NGDA) data from the U.S. Geological Survey, displays recreation structures in the U.S. This layer is checked weekly for updates.
properties.description:
This layer is derived from the Recreation Structures dataset hosted by Esri Federal Data and displays only Alaska features.

Recreation Structures
 
This feature layer, utilizing National Geospatial Data Asset (NGDA) data from the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS), displays recreation structures in the U.S. Per the USGS, “Structures data are designed to be used in general mapping and in the analysis of structure related activities using geographic information system technology. The National Map structures data is commonly combined with other data themes, such as boundaries, elevation, hydrography, and transportation, to produce general reference base maps.”
 
Headquarters & Picnic Areas (Core Banks, NC)
 
Data currency: This cached Esri federal service is checked weekly for updates from its enterprise federal source (Recreation) and will support mapping, analysis, data exports and OGC API – Feature access
NGDAID: 135 (USGS National Structures Dataset - USGS National Map Downloadable Data Collection)
OGC API Features Link: (Recreation Structures - OGC Features) copy this link to embed it in OGC Compliant viewers
For more information, please visit: The National Map

For feedback please contact: Esri_US_Federal_Data@esri.com

NGDA Data Set
 
This data set is part of the NGDA Real Property Theme Community. Per the Federal Geospatial Data Committee (FGDC), Real Property is defined as "the spatial representation (location) of real property entities, typically consisting of one or more of the following: unimproved land, a building, a structure, site improvements and the underlying land. Complex real property entities (that is "facilities") are used for a broad spectrum of functions or missions. This theme focuses on spatial representation of real property assets only and does not seek to describe special purpose functions of real property such as those found in the Cultural Resources, Transportation, or Utilities themes."
 
For other NGDA Content: Esri Federal Datasets

properties.snippet: Park facilities, park lands, facility rentals, projects and additional information from Anchorage Parks and Recreation
properties.description:
The Anchorage Parks and Recreation Department is responsible for beautifying, operating and maintaining Park and Recreation assets (parks, trails, community recreation centers and community pools) as well as implementing year-round recreation programs for all ages and caring for our natural resource areas.  The Department is also responsible for horticulture and park maintenance.  The Department provides support for community gardens, dog parks and Youth Employment in Parks (YEP). Additionally, one of the most important and exciting jobs for Parks and Recreation staff is working with Anchorage’s impressive numbers of volunteers. In 2013, over 6,000 volunteers contributed over 125,000 hours of service to the Parks and Recreation Department.

 

Please visit our website for more information at https://www.muni.org/Departments/parks/Pages/default.aspx or contact our office if you have any questions or comments at 907-343-4355.

properties.snippet: Explore an interactive map showing recreation opportunities in the Mat-Su Borough, including trails, winter grooming updates, and public waterbody access.
properties.description:
Waterbody Access: This data represents verified public access to waterbodies in the Mat-Su Borough, with associated amenities and known conditions. 

 

Trails: This data represents trail locations within the Matanuska - Susitna Borough. Some of the trails are on Borough lands and under Borough management authority, however many of the trails are not maintained by the Borough. These trails are a compilation of data from a variety of sources and contain detailed attributes such as development level, accessibility, seasonal availability, typical activities (e.g., hiking, biking, skiing, equestrian access, motorized use, etc). This trail layer supports planning, public access, emergency response, and recreational development and will promote regional trail connectivity, stewardship, and informed decision-making for residents, visitors, and land managers.

Winter Grooming: This data represents winter grooming updates for trails maintained by Mat-Su Borough staff or organizations in a Trail Partner Agreement with the Borough. Grooming may be optimized for cross-country skiing, dog mushing, snow-machining, or other activities depending on the area. Check area signage for any usage designations.

properties.snippet: Depicts the boundaries of the Kenai Peninsula Borough Recreation Service Areas, as described in Chapter 16 of the Kenai Peninsula Borough Code of Ordinances.
properties.description: There are currently two Recreation Service Areas within the Kenai Peninsula Borough, as identified within Chapter 16 of the Kenai Peninsula Borough Code of Ordinances - North Peninsula Recreation Service Area, and Seldovia Recreational Service Area. The board of directors of each service area supervise recreation services, facilities, and programs within each service area, including but not limited to senior citizen and youth programs, facility rentals, and other activities.
